title: Café De Unie, Rotterdam
lede: J. J. P. Oud’s 1925 café front, rebuilt in 1986: the building is a billboard of flat colored planes, yellow bars, and square capitals.
summary: Black, red-orange, white, blue, and yellow planes with capital lettering on a café facade. J. J. P. Oud, 1925; reconstruction 1986.
made: 1924–1925 (original on the Coolsingel, destroyed 1940); reconstruction 1985–1986 on the Mauritsweg

evidence.note: Inspected a 2009 photograph of the reconstruction by “Ad” on [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:WLANL_-_Adfoto_-_Caf%C3%A9_De_Unie,_JJP_Oud_(1925).jpg) (1920 × 2560 px, viewed at 1600 px). No image is stored. The photograph shows the 1986 reconstruction, not the 1925 building.

notice: The original building was destroyed on 14 May 1940. The existing facade is a reconstruction on a different street.

styles.note: De Stijl applied to a commercial front: flat rectangles in primaries, black, and white, with lettering built into the composition.

context: Oud designed the café for the Coolsingel in Rotterdam in 1924–1925. It was destroyed on 14 May 1940 and reconstructed in 1985–1986 by the architect Carel Weeber on the Mauritsweg. [archiweb](https://www.archiweb.cz/en/b/cafe-de-unie).
archiweb names Theo van Doesburg as a co-author; this record does not rely on that claim.
observed: A black band near the top carries “DE UNIE” in large light gray-blue capitals, with “CAFE” set vertically at both ends and a yellow bar above.
Below it a large red-orange plane carries raised lines that form nested right angles.
Yellow bars frame the upper window band and the lower windows; the lower windows have yellow inner frames.
A vertical sign reads “DE • UNIE” in blue capitals with a yellow strip; a tall blue sign at the left reads “CAFE RESTAURANT” twice.
The ground floor is framed in bright blue; the rest of the facade is white.
A dark later storey rises behind the facade, and ordinary brick buildings stand on both sides.
interpretation: The facade treats architecture as a graphic panel, which makes it the closest pre-war precedent for a De Stijl website or sign system.
The red is closer to orange in this photograph, which may reflect the reconstruction, weathering, or the camera.
borrow: Build the name into the composition as one rectangular plane among others.
Use thin yellow bars as frames and dividers between larger black, red, and white planes.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The Commons photograph is CC BY-SA 2.0, but Oud died in 1963, so his design is protected in the Netherlands until 2034. Dutch freedom of panorama would probably permit exterior photographs; the lead curator can decide.
